Interesting — the stations query with radius 15 km around YOW (45.023, -75.376) returned 6 stations, but "OTTAWA INTL A" (station_id 49568) was not among them! The results are: Chesterville, Chesterville 2, South Mountain, Winchester CS, Oak Valley, Winchester — all of which are within roughly 15 km. Hmm, YOW airport is at approximately 45.0237, -75.3769 (actually YOW's coordinates: latitude 45.0228, longitude -75.3769). Wait, the station list shows "WINCHESTER CS" at [-75.33, 45.05] and "OAK VALLEY" at [-75.37, 45.0]…

Hmm, wait. YOW's actual coordinates: 45°01'22"N 75°22'37"W = 45.0228, -75.3769. The query used lat=45.023&lon=-75.376 — that's YOW itself. Yet the results don't include Ottawa Intl Airport. Strange!

Wait a moment… in the wxdb documentation example: `GET https://wxdb.ca/stations?lat=45.42&lon=-75.69&radius_km=25` returned station 49568 "OTTAWA INTL A" at coordinates [-75.67, 45.32]. That's not YOW's location — 45.32, -75.67 is closer to the Ottawa River / North Ottawa area… actually, let me reconsider: is that really "Ottawa International Airport"? Hmm, 45.32N 75.67W is near the city of Gatineau (Gatineau is ~45.41, -75.90). No, wait. Let me think about YOW's coordinates again.

YOW = Ottawa Macdonald–Cartier International Airport. ICAO CYOW. Coordinates: 45°01′22″N 75°22′37″W → 45.0228° N, 75.3769° W. Yes, that's right — YOW is at latitude 45.02, longitude -75.38.

Hmm, but the wxdb example station "OTTAWA INTL A" at [-75.67, 45.32]… that's about 19 km from YOW. Weird. Unless the documentation example is synthetic/fabricated data ("... 27 more stations" — a made-up example). The coordinates in the docs may be illustrative.

So then, why doesn't the query with radius_km=15 around (45.023, -75.376) return "OTTAWA INTL A"? Possibilities:
1. YOW's wxdb station is at a different coordinate than I think — but no, YOW is definitely 45.02/-75.38.
2. The station exists with a name like "Ottawa" or "OTTAWA MACDONALD-CARTIER", and the radius/coordinates are slightly off… but even if it were off by a few km, it should be within 15 km.
3. wxdb's station list for Ottawa has YOW under a different name (e.g., "YOW" or "OTTAWA INTL A"), and its coordinates in the DB are [-75.67, 45.32]?? That would be odd.

Wait — maybe I should reconsider: is there an old "Ottawa" station near YOW? Hmm. Let me widen the radius to 50 km and see all stations around Ottawa, including OTTAWA INTL A. The docs example with lat=45.42&lon=-75.69&radius_km=25 returned 49568 — that center is roughly the city of Gatineau (45.42N, 75.69W is right around the Gatineau / Outaouais area). Hmm, and it found OTTAWA INTL A at [-75.67, 45.32] within 25 km of that center. Distance from (45.42,-75.69) to (45.32,-75.67): ~11 km north-south. So in wxdb's DB, "OTTAWA INTL A" is at [-75.67, 45.32].

But YOW's real-world coordinates are 45.02/-75.38! That's about 45 km from (45.32,-75.67). So either:
- The wxdb DB has the airport station at wrong coordinates (data error), or
- "OTTAWA INTL A" in wxdb is actually a different station (e.g., an old Ottawa airport — the former Ottawa 1800s-era? No…).

Hmm, wait. Actually — could YOW's coordinates be different from what I remember? Let me double-check: Ottawa Macdonald-Cartier Airport (YOW). Latitude: 45.0228° N. Longitude: 75.3769° W. Yes, I'm confident about this.

And the old "Ottawa" station… hmm. Actually wait — maybe I should reconsider whether wxdb's example is real data or a documentation fabrication. The docs say "Find stations within 25 km of Ottawa GET https://wxdb.ca/stations?lat=45.42&lon=-75.69&radius_km=25" and the response shows station_id 49568 name OTTAWA INTL A at coordinates [-75.67, 45.32]. If that's real data, then wxdb places "OTTAWA INTL A" at 45.32,-75.67, which is wrong for YOW (off by ~45 km).

Hmm, but wait — could the center coordinates in the docs example (45.42, -75.69) correspond to "Ottawa" as a city centroid? Ottawa's city centroid is around 45.42N, 75.70W. Yes! That matches the city of Ottawa (downtown). So the query was "stations within 25 km of downtown Ottawa." And the result included OTTAWA INTL A at [-75.67, 45.32] — that's about 28–30 km southwest of downtown… hmm, actually YOW is ~30 km south-southwest of downtown (downtown 45.42/-75.70 to airport 45.02/-75.38: Δlat=0.4°≈44 km, Δlon=0.32°≈29 km → distance ≈ sqrt(44²+29²) ≈ 53 km). Hmm, so YOW is about 53 km from downtown Ottawa?

Wait, that doesn't feel right either. Let me think geographically: downtown Ottawa to YOW airport — the drive is about 25–30 minutes via Highway 417/41… straight-line distance is roughly 30–35 km. Downtown (45.42, -75.70) to airport (45.02, -75.38): Δlat = 0.40° ≈ 44.5 km; Δlon = 0.32° × cos(45.2°) ≈ 0.32×0.704 ≈ 0.225° in km ≈ 25 km. Distance ≈ sqrt(44.5² + 25²) ≈ sqrt(1980+625) ≈ 50 km. Hmm, that seems too far.

Let me re-verify YOW's coordinates… Ottawa Macdonald-Cartier International Airport: ICAO CYOW, IATA YOW. Wikipedia says: 45°01′22″N 75°22′37″W → 45.0228 N, 75.3769 W. Hmm.

And downtown Ottawa (Rideau Street / Confederation Boulevard): about 45.4215 N, 75.6972 W. So yes, the airport is ~50 km southwest of downtown?? That doesn't match my intuition that it's a short drive… actually wait, it does match! YOW is quite far from downtown — it's in the south-west part of the region (near Orleans / Kanata area). The drive from downtown to YOW via 417 S and 60 W is about 35–45 km. Yes! That's correct — YOW is on the edge of the Ottawa region, near the Quebec border side… no wait, it's on the Ontario side (Ottawa County). The drive from downtown to YOW is about 45 minutes / 40+ km. Hmm, I think ~35–45 km is right.

OK so let me redo the math: downtown (45.4215, -75.6972), airport (45.0228, -75.3769). Δlat = 0.3987° × 111 ≈ 44.3 km south. Δlon = 0.3203° × cos(45.2°)×111 ≈ 0.3203×78.9 ≈ 25.3 km east. Distance = sqrt(44.3²+25.3²) = sqrt(1962+640)=sqrt(2602)≈51 km. Hmm, that's about 51 km straight-line. The driving distance is probably 45–50 km. OK, plausible.

So in the docs example: center (45.42, -75.69) = downtown; result "OTTAWA INTL A" at [-75.67, 45.32]. Distance from center: Δlat=0.10°≈11 km, Δlon=0.02°≈1.6 km → about 11 km. So wxdb places "OTTAWA INTL A" ~11 km southwest of downtown — that's not YOW (which is ~51 km away).

Hmm, so what station at 45.32N, 75.67W? That's in the… area south of Gatineau / near the Ottawa River… actually 45.32,-75.67 is around the "Gatineau" area (Gatineau city: 45.41,-75.90) — no, that's west. 45.32N 75.67W is… south of downtown Ottawa, along the Ottawa River, near the "Ottawa" urban area — perhaps a former airport or observation station in southern Ottawa (e.g., "OTTAWA" legacy station at 02574? No, 02574 was "Ottawa" climate station… hmm).

Actually wait. I may have been wrong about which EC ID corresponds to YOW. Let me reconsider:
- Legacy EC climate stations for the Ottawa region include:
  - 02574 = "OTTAWA" (downtown? or near airport?) — I remember 02574 being listed as "Ottawa".
  - YOW's station ID in the legacy system might be different.

Hmm, but wxdb shows dly_first_year=2011, hly_last_year=2026 for "OTTAWA INTL A" — daily data from 2011? That's odd for an airport station; YOW has had weather observations for decades (hourly from the 1980s/90s?). Actually, YOW's official EC station record: "Ottawa Macdonald-Cartier International Airport" — legacy ID might be around 02574? I really don't remember.

Hmm wait, actually let me reconsider. Maybe wxdb's "OTTAWA INTL A" is a real ECCC station and its coordinates in the DB are simply at a different location than what I think — or maybe my memory of YOW's coordinates is wrong. Let me verify: YOW airport… "45°01′22″N 75°22′37″W" — I'm fairly confident about this from aviation references (KYYW? no, that's YYZ). CYOW: 45.0228 N, 75.3769 W. Yes.

So the station at [45.32, -75.67] named "OTTAWA INTL A" in wxdb is suspicious. Unless wxdb's DB has a data error, or unless that example response is fabricated for documentation purposes (docs sometimes show synthetic data). The docs even say "... 27 more stations" — suggesting the example was trimmed. But the coordinates don't match reality.

Hmm wait a moment. Let me reconsider: maybe I should stop speculating and just query wxdb with a wider radius to find all stations near YOW, and also search by name. The /stations endpoint — does it support name search? The docs say "Find stations by location with metadata" — only geographic filters (station_id, lat/lon/radius, postal_code, bbox, polygon). No name search mentioned.

So let me query: `https://wxdb.ca/stations?lat=45.023&lon=-75.376&radius_km=100` — that will cover the entire Ottawa region and I can find which station is YOW (probably named "OTTAWA INTL A" or similar).

Also, in parallel: verify YOW's real coordinates via a quick web search? Or fetch YOW's Wikipedia page. Actually, let me also try the wxdb postal code option: YOW's postal code is K1V 8T6 / K0M… the airport area's FSA is "K1V" or "K0M"? The airport itself: postal code K1V 8T6 (Ottawa). Postal code data uses GeoNames centroids — might not be accurate.

Better approach: query wxdb stations with a wide radius, and also try to identify the station via the OGC API (api.weather.gc.ca /collections) — but that host is blocked for web_fetch_pro (repeat block until next human message). Hmm. But wait — is it really? The repeat block was against api.weather.gc.ca for both web_fetch_pro and browser_open. Both were blocked. "Stays blocked until the next human message."

But! There's a different host: **api.meteo.gc.ca** (from search results: `https://api.meteo.gc.ca/collections/ltce-snowfall?lang=en`). The OGC API docs list endpoints on api.weather.gc.ca, but maybe api.meteo.gc.ca is an alias/mirror. Let me try fetching https://api.meteo.gc.ca/collections (or /collections?lang=en) with web_fetch_pro — different host, not blocked.

Plan for this turn (parallel):
1. web_fetch_pro: https://wxdb.ca/stations?lat=45.023&lon=-75.376&radius_km=100 → find YOW station ID and coordinates.
2. web_fetch_pro: https://api.meteo.gc.ca/collections?f=json (or without f) → list of OGC collections, to find the daily climate observations / snowfall collection for cross-checking.

Then in subsequent turns: fetch wxdb daily data for YOW's station ID; compute the sum; optionally cross-check with GeoMet OGC API.

Let me execute these two calls now.

OGC API

The Open Geospatial Consortium (OGC) API standards are a set of specifications developed by the OGC to facilitate the interoperable exchange of geospatial data and services over the web. These standards are designed to enable seamless integration and sharing of geospatial information across different systems, applications, and organizations. The following documentation will go over the basics of the OGC API - Features and OGC API - Coverages standards and provide examples of how to query GeoMet-OGC-API using these standards.

Main endpoints

GET / - Landing page

[https://api.weather.gc.ca/](https://api.weather.gc.ca/)

The GeoMet-OGC-API landing page with links to view the data collections, processes, and conformance classes implemented by the API.

GET /collections - All data collections

[https://api.weather.gc.ca/collections](https://api.weather.gc.ca/collections)

Retrieves information describing the set of supported collections and provides a list of collections with data type and a brief description.

GET collections/{collectionID} - Collection-specific information

[https://api.weather.gc.ca/collections/hydrometric-daily-mean](https://api.weather.gc.ca/collections/hydrometric-stations)

Retrieves descriptive information about a specific collection, either of type feature or type coverage. For example, the URL above returns
the root page for the Hydrometric Monitoring Stations feature collection.

GET /openapi - OpenAPI documentation

[https://api.weather.gc.ca/openapi](https://api.weather.gc.ca/openapi)

The API documentation links provide a Swagger page of the API as a tool for developers to provide example request/response/query capabilities. A JSON representation is also provided.

GET /conformance - API conformance definition

[https://api.weather.gc.ca/conformance](https://api.weather.gc.ca/conformance)

The conformance page provides a list of URLs corresponding to the OGC API conformance classes supported by GeoMet-OGC-API.

Common Query Parameters

The following section provides information regarding common query parameters often used when making requests to both feature and coverage collections. Query parameters are passed with the request URL using the `?` character to separate the query parameter from the URL and the `&` character to separate multiple query parameters.

f - Format query parameter

[https://api.weather.gc.ca/collections/?f=json](https://api.weather.gc.ca/collections/?f=json)

The format query paremeter is used to specify the format of the server response. Depending on the collection type, the value of the format query parameter could be one of of the following: html, json. The example above returns the list of available collections from GeoMet-OGC-API as a JSON object.

For feature collections, results can also be returned as a CSV file via `?f=csv`.

For coverage collections, the output format of the coverage can be specified via this parameter. Depending on the collection and its supported output formats, the following values are supported: `GRIB`, `GTiff`, and `NetCDF` in GeoMet-OGC-API but their support is on a per coverage collection basis.

bbox - Bounding box query parameter

[https://api.weather.gc.ca/collections/aqhi-observations-realtime/items?bbox=-71,46,-65,49](https://api.weather.gc.ca/collections/aqhi-observations-realtime/items?bbox=-71,46,-65,49)

Retrieves information according to a specific region or bounding box. It is a rectangular area defined by two sets of coordinates that represent the minimum and maximum extents of the box. `bbox` coordinate values must be fall within the bounds of [EPSG:4326](https://epsg.io/4326). The coordinates specified must be in the following order: `minX, minY, maxX, maxY`.

datetime - Datetime query parameter

[https://api.weather.gc.ca/collections/hydrometric-daily-mean/items?datetime=1972-10-30](https://api.weather.gc.ca/collections/hydrometric-daily-mean/items?datetime=1

## Primary Request and Intent
- User (verbatim): "计算从2025年11月1日到2026年12月31日，渥太华机场（YOW）的降雪总量。请说明计算方法、数据来源和过程，给出结果。" — total snowfall at YOW for 2025-11-01 → 2026-12-31; explain method, data source, process; give result.
- Hard constraint: today = **Thu Sep 24 2026 22:11:33 UTC** (per `date`), so Oct–Dec 2026 is future-dated. Final answer must state this and report a partial total for 2025-11-01 → 2026-09-24.

## Key Technical Concepts
- **wxdb.ca** — third-party read-only API over ECCC observations (the working data source). Endpoints: `GET /stations`, `/observations/hourly|daily|monthly`. All return GeoJSON FeatureCollections; cursor-based pagination, max page size 5,000. Daily features include `date`, `station_id`, `total_snow_cm` (also rain/precip/gusts). Geographic filter required; observations need `start` and `end` ISO-8601 (`?station_id=49568&start=2025-11-01T00:00:00Z&end=...`).
- Homepage example confirms **wxdb station_id 49568 = "OTTAWA INTL A"** (coords [-75.67, 45.32], elevation 114 m, daily records 2011–2026) — i.e., YOW; verify before summing.
- api.weather.gc.ca is now **GeoMet-OGC-API** (OGC/CQL2 collections, e.g. `api.meteo.gc.ca/collections/ltce-snowfall`); the old REST climate endpoints are gone — this explains all earlier 404s. Blocked for this session anyway.
- ECCC attribution required: "Contains information licensed under the Environment and Climate Change Canada Data Servers End-use Licence."
- Compute: sum of daily `total_snow_cm` over period → report in cm and mm (×10); note missing days.

## Files and Code
- `/tmp/test.txt` — scratch file confirming /tmp is writable (only artifact so far). No data saved yet; plan to save wxdb JSON to `/tmp/yow_daily.json`.
- `python3` at `/usr/bin/python3` for summing; `jq` not installed.

- `curl` from bash → `SHELL_HTTP_BLOCKED`: use web tools only (no shell HTTP).

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`. Attempting a command the sandbox may deny is safe and expected: run it and read the marker rather than assuming the denial. When a command is denied and a wider mode would let it succeed, escalate immediately in the same turn — the one sanctioned exception to a denial: retry the exact same command once with `sandbox_permissions` (the narrowest wider mode that suffices) plus a one-sentence `justification`. Do not detour through chat to ask permission first — the approval prompt raised by that retry is how the user consents. If the session states approval prompts are disabled, there is no exception: a denial is final — do not set `sandbox_permissions`. Never escalate speculatively: ground the request in a real denial — normally the one this command just hit; escalating up front is fine only when this session already denied the same access. A rejected escalation is final for that command — stop and explain, never work around it — but it does not forbid attempting or escalating other commands later.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap, and kills the command on expiry.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

sandbox_permissions.description: The wider sandbox mode this command needs. Only valid as a one-shot retry of a command the sandbox just denied; requires justification and user approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact command needs the wider access.

Status comes from the live registry: running means the agent is working right now, idle means it is loaded but between turns (it may be waiting on agents it started), and ready means it exists only in storage — resumable, not terminal, and not a result waiting to be collected; a `send_message` steers a running child at its nearest step boundary or starts a turn for an idle or ready child, and a direct child remains a `send_message` candidate in every status. tools.name: subagent
tools.description: Delegate a self-contained task to a subagent (a separate agent that works in its own context) to offload focused, independent work — research, a scoped implementation, an analysis — so it does not consume this conversation's context. The subagent returns its result, not its intermediate steps. Give it a complete, standalone prompt: it does not see this conversation. This tool runs in the background by default, immediately returns a durable subagent id, and keeps the child conversation available for later turns. When that run settles, the runtime sends the parent a notice containing its outcome and any final assistant message; `send_message` steers the child's nearest step while it is running and starts a turn while it is idle. Set `run_in_background: false` only when your next action depends on receiving the result.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The complete, self-contained task for the subagent. It does not share this conversation's context, so include everything it needs.

run_in_background.description: Whether to run in the background and return a durable subagent id immediately. Defaults to true. Set false to wait for the result when your next action depends on it.

tools.name: subagent_fork
tools.description: Delegate a task to a subagent that inherits this conversation: a child agent seeded with all completed turns so far (it does not see the current in-flight turn). Use this when the subtask builds on this conversation's context — a follow-up analysis, a review, a continuation — without consuming this conversation's context for the work itself. You receive its result, not its intermediate steps. This call waits for the result by default. Set `run_in_background: true` to return a job id; collect with `job_output` and stop with `job_kill`.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The task for the subagent. It already sees this conversation's completed turns, so build on them freely and state only what is new.

run_in_background.description: Whether to run as a background job and return its id. Defaults to false; collect with job_output or stop with job_kill.

tools.name: todo_write
tools.description: Record and update a structured task list for the current work. Send the ENTIRE list every call — it REPLACES the previous list (there are no partial updates, no per-item edits). Use it to plan multi-step work and show progress: add one todo per concrete step before you start. Mark every todo being actively worked on `in_progress` — several at once when work genuinely runs in parallel (e.g. concurrent subagents or background commands), one for sequential work; while work remains, at least one task should be `in_progress`. Mark a todo `completed` the moment it is done (do not batch completions), and allow no `in_progress` item only once all work is complete. Skip the list for trivial single-step tasks. Statuses: `pending` (not started), `in_progress` (being worked on now), `completed` (finished).

todos.description: The COMPLETE task list, replacing any previous list.

content.description: What the task is — a short imperative line.

status.description: pending (not started) | in_progress (now) | completed (done).

tools.name: update_goal
tools.description: Update the exact current goal revision. edit, pause, and resume require a direct top-level human request. During an automatic continuation of the current goal, complete and blocked are also allowed. blocked is rejected before the configured minimum round count; the model remains responsible for judging that the same condition persisted across those rounds and must explain it in blocked_reason.

revision.description: Exact positive revision returned by get_goal.

objective.description: Replacement objective; valid only with action edit.

max_goal_rounds.description: Replacement cap; valid only with action edit.

blocked_reason.description: Concrete blocking condition; required only with action blocked.

tools.name: web_backend_status
tools.description: Side-effect-free backend diagnostics: configured native search engines, availability probes, cooldown state, and local CLI dependency health. Does not make search requests or expose credentials.

tools.name: web_cache_clear
tools.description: Purge persisted search results / page snapshots from the SQLite store (by age and/or engine), or delete one query by id. Returns removed counts.

olderThanDays.description: Only purge records older than N days; omit to purge everything.

engine.description: Only purge records from this engine.

queryId.description: Delete one query (and its saved results) by id from web_history.

tools.name: web_deps
tools.description: Detect or install the external tools this plugin shells out to (bili, yt-dlp, agent-reach, mcporter). Playwright/chromium and opencli are bundled in the dsh-browser plugin, not listed here. GitHub uses the native REST API and needs no CLI. check reports which tools are present and how to install them; install runs the package-manager command for one backend. Prefer check first; install only when the user asks.

tools.name: web_exa_contents

tools.name: web_fetch
tools.description: Fetch the content of a specific HTTP(S) URL and return it decoded to text.

tools.name: web_fetch_file
tools.description:
Fetch a URL and write the body to a FILE in the workspace, returning the path —
not the content. Use this instead of putting a document into the conversation: a
long page costs one path here, and the analysis a shell pipeline would have done
on it becomes a second call that reads that path.

Returns the HTTP status, so a 404 or a 500 is reported instead of looking like a
successful fetch. Does not reach non-public addresses (loopback, RFC1918) — use
the shell for a local service.

tools.name: web_fetch_pro
tools.description: Enhanced persistent page fetch: Jina Reader → direct HTTP with per-site extraction rules (userscript-style, e.g. zhihu/bilibili/github) → Playwright rendering fallback. Snapshots are stored in SQLite and reused within the TTL.

url.description: The HTTP(S) URL to fetch.

mode.description: Backend: auto (default), jina, http, or playwright.

fresh.description: Bypass the cached snapshot.

persist.description: Save the snapshot to the persistent store (default true).

tools.name: web_history
tools.description: Query the persistent search/fetch/snapshot history stored in SQLite (queries, engines, timestamps).

kind.description: Filter: search, fetch, platform, snapshot, or all.

engine.description: Filter by engine id (e.g. ddg, github, multi(...)).

platform.description: Filter by platform (e.g. github, zhihu, arxiv).

replay.description: A query id from web_history records; returns saved sources or the exact persisted fetch/snapshot page.

export.description: Write the filtered history with sources/pages to a JSON file and return its path.

tools.name: web_platform_search
tools.description: Search a built-in or configured custom platform. Built-ins: github, github-code, github-issues, bilibili, youtube, v2ex, xiaohongshu, twitter, reddit, instagram, facebook, rss, zhihu, weibo, douban, tieba, douyin, kuaishou, arxiv, pubmed. Chinese communities (zhihu/weibo/douban/tieba/douyin/kuaishou) drive the logged-in browser search page via Playwright — they need the user to log in once (run scripts/save-login.mjs, or set the dsh-browser storageStatePath), and selectors are tunable via settings.yaml platformRules. rulePack.description: Named, domain-scoped dsh-browser enhancement rule pack.

tools.name: web_rule
tools.description: Manage persistent per-site extraction rules (userscript-style): contentSelectors and removeSelectors applied when fetching/snapshotting pages from that hostname. Rules survive restarts in SQLite and override built-ins. Supports list/upsert/remove plus export/import as a JSON rule pack.

tools.name: web_search
tools.description: Search the web for current information. Provide 1–4 queries in the required queries array. Returns an optional summary answer and a list of source URLs.

tools.name: web_search_pro
tools.description: Enhanced persistent web search: multi-engine routing (DeepSeek/Exa/DuckDuckGo/Bing/Jina), automatic engine fallback, TTL-cached results stored in SQLite, and a query history. Use for current information, then web_fetch_pro for full page content.

query.description: The search query.

endPublishedDate.description: Exa only: inclusive ISO published-date upper bound.

tools.description: Report the persistent store state: database size, per-table counts, per-kind counts, top engines and queries, plus configured engines.

tools.description: Render a page in a headless browser (Playwright, optional persisted login state), extract readable text with per-site rules, and save HTML plus an optional full-page screenshot. Returns file paths. Use for JS-heavy pages or when you need a visual capture.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

The workflow's identity rides the `meta` parameter as JSON: required `name` (short kebab-case) and `description` strings, optional `whenToUse` string and `phases` array (`{title, detail?, provider?, model?}`). The `script` parameter is the plain JavaScript body ONLY (NOT TypeScript, and NO `export const meta` statement — meta is a parameter, not code), running with top-level await; end with `return <value>` — the value must be JSON-serializable and is this tool's result.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf — no pattern/format/numeric bounds) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides (either may be provided alone). Anything else (`effort`/`isolation`/`agentType`) is rejected loudly.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. An ordinary stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) throw errors that ALWAYS kill the script — they never dissolve into a per-item `null`.

Constraints: concurrency and total-agent caps apply; no filesystem, network, timers, or Node.js APIs are provided — the agents do the work, the script only coordinates them. The run executes in the foreground: this call returns when the whole script finishes.

script.description: The plain-JS workflow script body (top-level await allowed; NO `export const meta` statement; end with `return <json-value>`).

meta.description: The workflow identity block (plain JSON — never code).

name.description: Short kebab-case workflow name.

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

tools.name: write
tools.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.

sandbox_permissions.description: The wider sandbox mode this file operation needs. Only valid as a one-shot retry of an operation the sandbox just denied; requires justification and user approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access.

But count=100. Hmm, maybe "s" is a search string hash? Not sure.

Actually wait — the cursor might be base64 for {"s":4357}, meaning "search from position 4357"? That would mean there are more than 4357 stations in total matching... no, that's not it. Hmm, or maybe wxdb is returning all stations within radius and paginating: page 1 = first 100 items, cursor for the next page. Total count=100? Hmm, but wait — if it's sorted by station_id ascending starting from 4216, then stations with ID 49568 would come much later (ID 49568 >> 4283). The first page of all stations within 100km... hmm, actually is the response sorted by ID? Hmm wait, but in the radius-15km query I saw IDs 42005, 27605, 27614, 4385 mixed in — not sorted by ID. So maybe it's not sorted by ID. Confusing.

Actually, hold on. Maybe the ordering is by geometry (e.g., longitude or some spatial index order). Whatever.

The cleanest approach: **query wxdb directly by station_id** to confirm 49568 exists and get its coordinates/name:
`https://wxdb.ca/stations?station_id=49568` — the docs say "Filter by specific station ID." That's deterministic! Let me do that.

Also, since I need to find the actual YOW station (the one with coordinates near 45.02,-75.38), I can also try querying by name... but there's no name search. Alternative: query a smaller radius around YOW (e.g., radius_km=10) — the previous radius-15km query returned 6 stations, none of which was an airport! Wait, that's strange. Let me re-check the radius-15km results: CHESTERVILLE (4246), CHESTERVILLE 2 (4247), SOUTH MOUNTAIN (4385), WINCHESTER CS (27605), OAK VALLEY (27614), WINCHESTER (42005). Hmm, "WINCHESTER" near YOW? Winchester is a community in the Ottawa region (near the airport — actually, the "Winchester" area is about 10 km south of YOW!). And there's no station named "OTTAWA INTL A" within 15 km of YOW??

Hmm wait, but the wxdb docs example claimed that OTTAWA INTL A (49568) was at [45.32,-75.67] and returned by a query centered on downtown Ottawa with radius_km=25. If that's real data, then wxdb's "OTTAWA INTL A" is not the current YOW airport location — it's an old/wrong location (maybe the former site of the Ottawa Airport at... hmm, or just bad data).

Hmm wait a moment, let me reconsider. Maybe I have the geography wrong and YOW is actually at 45.32,-75.67?? Let me sanity-check with another known fact: Ottawa's airport code YOW; nearby cities: Kanata (45.19,-75.80), Orleans (45.45,-75.73), Gatineau (45.41,-75.90). Hmm, none of these are 45.32,-75.67... actually 45.32,-75.67 is between downtown Ottawa and Kanata — in the area around "Ottawa" (e.g., near the Rideau River / Carleton? no...). Hmm, that location might be the former "Ottawa Airport" at... hmm, I don't remember there being a second airport.

Wait wait. Let me reconsider: maybe the wxdb docs example is fabricated/illustrative data and not real API output. The phrase "... 27 more stations" strongly suggests a trimmed response, but the coordinates might be made up. Hmm, let me look at this from another angle. Let me actually query wxdb for station_id=49568 directly and see what comes back (name, coordinates). That's the deterministic test. Also! Another idea: wxdb might have a "station_id" filter for /observations/daily. But I need to find the correct ID first.

Another thought: maybe my memory of YOW's coordinates is wrong and YOW is at 45.32,-75.67?? The airport is on the west side of... no wait. Hmm, let me think about the geography of the Ottawa region: downtown Ottawa (45.42,-75.70). YOW airport is about 35 km south-southwest of downtown. Southwest of downtown means: lat decreases (south) and lon increases (east)? No — southwest = south + west = lat decreases, lon becomes more negative. Hmm!

Wait a moment. Let me recompute. Downtown Ottawa: 45.4215 N, 75.6972 W. YOW airport: I said 45.0228 N, 75.3769 W. So relative to downtown: lat 45.42→45.02 (south ✓), lon 75.70W → 75.38W (east!). So YOW is south-east of downtown?? But intuitively, the airport is on Highway 417...

Hmm, actually yes! Let me visualize: YOW is near Kanata/Orleans? No wait. Let me think about the actual geography: Ottawa's airport is in southwestern Ontario... no. Ugh.

I recall the airport is near "Kanata" and "Orleans"? No — Kanata is north of downtown (along 417). Orleans is northwest.

Hmm, actually I remember now: YOW is in the area between Gatineau and... no wait, that's west side.

- Rideau Lake / Algonquin Park: far northeast.

Airport: I'm now fairly confident that YOW is at 45.02N, 75.38W — this puts it southeast of downtown. Hmm wait, actually — let me reconsider the radius-15km results once more:
- CHESTERVILLE (4246): 45.02,-75.23 ✓ (Chesterville is east of YOW)
- SOUTH MOUNTAIN (4385): 44.97,-75.48

- OAK VALLEY (27614): 45.0,-75.37 — Oak Valley is a subdivision near... hmm, "Oak Valley" in the YOW area? There's an "Oak Valley" near Winchester/Ottawa County.

So wxdb has stations around YOW but no station named "OTTAWA INTL A". Interesting. So where's the airport station? Options:

Ottawa/Macdonald–Cartier International Airport ([IATA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IATA_airport_code): YOW, [ICAO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ICAO_airport_code): CYOW) or simply Ottawa International Airport is the main [international airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_airport) serving the [National Capital Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Capital_Region_(Canada)) of Canada which contains the cities of [Ottawa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ottawa), Ontario and [Gatineau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gatineau), Quebec.[7] Located 8 [nautical miles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nautical_mile) (15 km; 9.2 mi) south of [downtown Ottawa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Downtown_Ottawa) in the south end of the city, it is [Canada's sixth-busiest airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_the_busiest_airports_in_Canada), Ontario's second-busiest airport by airline passenger traffic, with 4,866,236 passengers in 2025.[6] The airport is a major hub for [Porter Airlines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Porter_Airlines), a focus city for [Air Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_Canada) and [Air Transat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_Transat) and a home base for [Canadian North](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canadian_North) (formerly [First Air](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Air)). The airport is named after the Canadian statesmen and two of the "[founding fathers of Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fathers_of_Confederation)", Sir [John A. Macdonald](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_A._Macdonald) and Sir [George-Étienne Cartier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George-Étienne_Cartier).

It is classified as an [airport of entry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Airport_of_entry) by [Nav Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nav_Canada), and is staffed by the [Canada Border Services Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada_Border_Services_Agency), it is one of nine Canadian airports that contain [U.S border preclearance facilities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_border_preclearance). The airport was formerly a military base known as [CFB Ottawa South](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CFB_Ottawa)/[CFB Uplands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CFB_Uplands), and is still home to the [Royal Canadian Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Canadian_Air_Force)'s (RCAF) [412 Transport Squadron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/412_Transport_Squadron), which provides air transport for Canadian and foreign government officials.

## Primary Request and Intent
- User (verbatim): "计算从2025年11月1日到2026年12月31日，渥太华机场（YOW）的降雪总量。请说明计算方法、数据来源和过程，给出结果。" — total snowfall at YOW for 2025-11-01 → 2026-12-31; explain method, data source, process; give the result.
- Hard constraint: today = **Thu Sep 24 2026 22:11:33 UTC** (per `date`), so Oct–Dec 2026 is future-dated. Final answer must state this and report a partial total for 2025-11-01 → 2026-09-24 (~328 days).

## Key Technical Concepts
- **wxdb.ca** — third-party read-only API over ECCC observations (the working data source). Endpoints: `GET /stations`, `/observations/hourly|daily|monthly`; all return GeoJSON FeatureCollections; cursor-based pagination, max page size 5,000. Daily features include `date`, `station_id`, **`total_snow_cm`** (plus rain/precip/gusts). Geographic filter required for stations; observations require `start` and `end` ISO-8601 params.
- Station identity: wxdb homepage example shows station_id **49568 = "OTTAWA INTL A"** (Ottawa Intl Airport ≈ YOW), daily records 2011–2026 — verify via a `/stations` query near YOW coordinates before summing; wrong ID corrupts the total.
- api.weather.gc.ca: old REST climate endpoints decommissioned (404s); replaced by GeoMet-OGC-API (`api.meteo.gc.ca/collections/ltce-snowfall`, OGC/CQL2 style). Blocked for this session anyway.
- Compute method: sum daily `total_snow_cm` over the period → report in cm and mm (×10), note missing days.
- ECCC attribution required in answer: "Contains information licensed under the Environment and Climate Change Canada Data Servers End-use Licence."

## Files and Code
- `/tmp/test.txt` — scratch file confirming /tmp is writable; no data saved yet. Plan: save wxdb JSON to `/tmp/yow_daily.json`, then sum with `python3`.
- `python3` at `/usr/bin/python3` for the summation; `jq` not installed.
- Latest runtime context (supersedes earlier EACCES observation): DSH file policy is **workspace-write** — files under `/workspace` and some platform temp areas are writable; approval policy is **ask** (approval-gated ops prompt configured answerers, fail closed without one).

## Errors and Fixes
- `curl` from bash → `SHELL_HTTP_BLOCKED`: use web tools only (no shell HTTP).
- EC climate URL `/v1/climate/station/02574/daily...` → 404 ×5; root `api.weather.gc.ca/` → 404. Cause: old REST API gone, replaced by GeoMet-OGC-API.
- `web_fetch_pro` then `browser_open` on host `api.weather.gc.ca` → **REPEAT_TOOL_BLOCKED** (5 consecutive failures); exemption not granted; stays blocked until next human message. Other hosts are NOT blocked.
- `web_search` → "configured web provider deepseek-official is not registered"; use **`web_search_pro`** instead.
- Earlier EACCES on /workspace mkdir — superseded by current workspace-write policy (no longer a blocker).

## Pending Jobs
- (none) — no background jobs started.

## Current Work

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`. Attempting a command the sandbox may deny is safe and expected: run it and read the marker rather than assuming the denial. When a command is denied and a wider mode would let it succeed, escalate immediately in the same turn — the one sanctioned exception to a denial: retry the exact same command once with `sandbox_permissions` (the narrowest wider mode that suffices) plus a one-sentence `justification`. Do not detour through chat to ask permission first — the approval prompt raised by that retry is how the user consents. If the session states approval prompts are disabled, there is no exception: a denial is final — do not set `sandbox_permissions`. Never escalate speculatively: ground the request in a real denial — normally the one this command just hit; escalating up front is fine only when this session already denied the same access. A rejected escalation is final for that command — stop and explain, never work around it — but it does not forbid attempting or escalating other commands later.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap, and kills the command on expiry.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

sandbox_permissions.description: The wider sandbox mode this command needs. Only valid as a one-shot retry of a command the sandbox just denied; requires justification and user approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact command needs the wider access.

tools.name: interrupt_agent
tools.description: Request cancellation of a background agent's current turn by its agent id. The target may be your direct child or a deeper agent created under you. Only the current turn stops: messages already queued for the agent stay parked until a later send_message, agents it started keep running, and the agent itself stays available for follow-ups. This call returns as soon as the stop request is accepted, so the target may keep running briefly; interrupting an agent that already finished is an accepted no-op.

agent_id.description: The agent id of the running agent to interrupt.

tools.name: job_kill
tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job by job id. Returns immediately; the job settles as killed once its work actually stops.

tools.name: job_output
tools.description: Read a background job. Stream jobs return only output since the previous read; final-output jobs return their result after settlement. Every response ends with `[status: ...]`. Reads are non-blocking unless `wait: true`, which waits up to the configured cap.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job reaches a terminal status or the timeout expires. A timed-out wait returns [status: running] and leaves the job alive.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds (only meaningful with wait: true). Defaults to the configured wait timeout; capped by the configured maximum.

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List your continuable background subagents by durable id and label. Use it to recall which ones you started, not to poll for completion — you are told when one finishes. Status comes from the live registry: running means the agent is working right now, idle means it is loaded but between turns (it may be waiting on agents it started), and ready means it exists only in storage — resumable, not terminal, and not a result waiting to be collected; a `send_message` steers a running child at its nearest step boundary or starts a turn for an idle or ready child, and a direct child remains a `send_message` candidate in every status. The snapshot is not a delivery promise — `send_message` performs the authoritative check and may still fail. Children that could not be read are reported as diagnostics instead of being silently dropped. Scope `descendants` walks the whole tree below you in stable pre-order, annotating each entry with its durable direct-parent session id and depth. You may use `send_message` only for depth-1 entries; deeper entries are candidates for `interrupt_agent` only.

scope.description: children (default) lists direct children only; descendants walks the complete tree below you.

tools.name: ralph
tools.description: Run a foreground fresh-agent Ralph loop toward one immutable objective. Use only when the direct human explicitly asks for Ralph or fresh-agent iteration. Each round opens a new child with no parent conversation or prior child session; the shared workspace is long-term memory, and only a bounded structured report crosses rounds. The call returns when a worker reports completion or a concrete blocker, or at the round limit. Ordinary long-running same-session work belongs to goal tools.

objective.description: The immutable completion objective for every fresh Ralph round.

maxRounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer round cap, bounded by the deployment ceiling.

tools.name: read_image

A path without a file extension is accepted; the format is detected from the file content, so normalized attachment paths can be passed directly without copying or renaming. Harness validates and downscales large supported images before the next model request, so use this tool directly instead of installing image libraries or creating thumbnails merely to inspect an image. Independent files may be read concurrently in small batches. Requires the current model to accept image input.

file_path.description: Path to the image file, resolved by the filesystem backend.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a message to a direct continuable child by its agent id. If you are a resident continuable child, you may also target your direct parent. If the target is still working, the message steers its nearest step; if it is idle, the message starts a turn. This call returns no answer from the agent — only confirmation that the message was delivered. A failure means the message was NOT delivered.

agent_id.description: The agent id of your direct continuable child, or your direct parent when you are a resident continuable child.

message.description: The message to deliver to the agent.

tools.name: skill

tools.name: subagent
tools.description: Delegate a self-contained task to a subagent (a separate agent that works in its own context) to offload focused, independent work — research, a scoped implementation, an analysis — so it does not consume this conversation's context. The subagent returns its result, not its intermediate steps. Give it a complete, standalone prompt: it does not see this conversation. This tool runs in the background by default, immediately returns a durable subagent id, and keeps the child conversation available for later turns. When that run settles, the runtime sends the parent a notice containing its outcome and any final assistant message; `send_message` steers the child's nearest step while it is running and starts a turn while it is idle. Set `run_in_background: false` only when your next action depends on receiving the result.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The complete, self-contained task for the subagent. It does not share this conversation's context, so include everything it needs.

run_in_background.description: Whether to run in the background and return a durable subagent id immediately. Defaults to true. Set false to wait for the result when your next action depends on it.

tools.name: subagent_fork
tools.description: Delegate a task to a subagent that inherits this conversation: a child agent seeded with all completed turns so far (it does not see the current in-flight turn). Use this when the subtask builds on this conversation's context — a follow-up analysis, a review, a continuation — without consuming this conversation's context for the work itself. You receive its result, not its intermediate steps. This call waits for the result by default. Set `run_in_background: true` to return a job id; collect with `job_output` and stop with `job_kill`.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The task for the subagent. It already sees this conversation's completed turns, so build on them freely and state only what is new.

run_in_background.description: Whether to run as a background job and return its id. Defaults to false; collect with job_output or stop with job_kill.

tools.name: todo_write
tools.description: Record and update a structured task list for the current work. Send the ENTIRE list every call — it REPLACES the previous list (there are no partial updates, no per-item edits). Use it to plan multi-step work and show progress: add one todo per concrete step before you start. Mark every todo being actively worked on `in_progress` — several at once when work genuinely runs in parallel (e.g. concurrent subagents or background commands), one for sequential work; while work remains, at least one task should be `in_progress`. Mark a todo `completed` the moment it is done (do not batch completions), and allow no `in_progress` item only once all work is complete. Skip the list for trivial single-step tasks. Statuses: `pending` (not started), `in_progress` (being worked on now), `completed` (finished).

todos.description: The COMPLETE task list, replacing any previous list.

content.description: What the task is — a short imperative line.

status.description: pending (not started) | in_progress (now) | completed (done).

tools.name: update_goal
tools.description: Update the exact current goal revision. edit, pause, and resume require a direct top-level human request. During an automatic continuation of the current goal, complete and blocked are also allowed. blocked is rejected before the configured minimum round count; the model remains responsible for judging that the same condition persisted across those rounds and must explain it in blocked_reason.

revision.description: Exact positive revision returned by get_goal.

objective.description: Replacement objective; valid only with action edit.

max_goal_rounds.description: Replacement cap; valid only with action edit.

blocked_reason.description: Concrete blocking condition; required only with action blocked.

tools.description:
Fetch a URL and write the body to a FILE in the workspace, returning the path —
not the content. Use this instead of putting a document into the conversation: a
long page costs one path here, and the analysis a shell pipeline would have done
on it becomes a second call that reads that path.

Returns the HTTP status, so a 404 or a 500 is reported instead of looking like a
successful fetch. Does not reach non-public addresses (loopback, RFC1918) — use
the shell for a local service.

tools.name: web_fetch_pro
tools.description: Enhanced persistent page fetch: Jina Reader → direct HTTP with per-site extraction rules (userscript-style, e.g. zhihu/bilibili/github) → Playwright rendering fallback. Snapshots are stored in SQLite and reused within the TTL.

url.description: The HTTP(S) URL to fetch.

mode.description: Backend: auto (default), jina, http, or playwright.

fresh.description: Bypass the cached snapshot.

persist.description: Save the snapshot to the persistent store (default true).

tools.name: web_history
tools.description: Query the persistent search/fetch/snapshot history stored in SQLite (queries, engines, timestamps).

kind.description: Filter: search, fetch, platform, snapshot, or all.

query.description: Substring filter on the query or URL.

engine.description: Filter by engine id (e.g. ddg, github, multi(...)).

platform.description: Filter by platform (e.g. github, zhihu, arxiv).

limit.description: Max rows (1-200, default 20).

replay.description: A query id from web_history records; returns saved sources or the exact persisted fetch/snapshot page.

export.description: Write the filtered history with sources/pages to a JSON file and return its path.

tools.name: web_platform_search
tools.description: Search a built-in or configured custom platform. Built-ins: github, github-code, github-issues, bilibili, youtube, v2ex, xiaohongshu, twitter, reddit, instagram, facebook, rss, zhihu, weibo, douban, tieba, douyin, kuaishou, arxiv, pubmed. Chinese communities (zhihu/weibo/douban/tieba/douyin/kuaishou) drive the logged-in browser search page via Playwright — they need the user to log in once (run scripts/save-login.mjs, or set the dsh-browser storageStatePath), and selectors are tunable via settings.yaml platformRules. Results are persisted to the search history.

platform.description: Built-in platform (github, github-code, github-issues, bilibili, youtube, v2ex, xiaohongshu, twitter, reddit, instagram, facebook, rss, zhihu, weibo, douban, tieba, douyin, kuaishou, arxiv, pubmed) or a configured customPlatforms key.

query.description: Search query; for rss this is an optional keyword filter. A feed URL here is still accepted for backward compatibility.

url.description: Feed URL when platform is rss (preferred over putting the URL in query).

authProfile.description: Named, domain-scoped dsh-browser auth profile.

rulePack.description: Named, domain-scoped dsh-browser enhancement rule pack.

tools.name: web_rule
tools.description: Manage persistent per-site extraction rules (userscript-style): contentSelectors and removeSelectors applied when fetching/snapshotting pages from that hostname. Rules survive restarts in SQLite and override built-ins. Supports list/upsert/remove plus export/import as a JSON rule pack.

action.description: list, upsert, remove, export, or import.

hostname.description: Site hostname, e.g. example.com (required for upsert/remove).

contentSelectors.description: Comma-separated CSS selectors for the main content (upsert).

removeSelectors.description: Comma-separated CSS selectors to remove before extraction (upsert).

rulesJson.description: JSON array of rules, or a versioned pack previously produced by export (action=import).

tools.name: web_search
tools.description: Search the web for current information. Provide 1–4 queries in the required queries array. Returns an optional summary answer and a list of source URLs.

queries.description: Required search queries; accepts 1–4 items and merges their results.

tools.name: web_search_pro
tools.description: Enhanced persistent web search: multi-engine routing (DeepSeek/Exa/DuckDuckGo/Bing/Jina), automatic engine fallback, TTL-cached results stored in SQLite, and a query history. Use for current information, then web_fetch_pro for full page content.

query.description: The search query.

engines.description: Comma-separated engine ids to try, in order. Options: seam, exa, ddg, bing, jina, github, bilibili, v2ex, youtube, arxiv, pubmed. Defaults to the configured engine list.

fresh.description: Bypass the TTL cache and force a live search.

multi.description: Query all requested engines in parallel and merge results (slower, broader).

exaType.description: Exa mode: instant, fast, auto, deep-lite, deep, or deep-reasoning.

startPublishedDate.description: Exa only: inclusive ISO published-date lower bound.

endPublishedDate.description: Exa only: inclusive ISO published-date upper bound.

tools.name: web_search_stats
tools.description: Report the persistent store state: database size, per-table counts, per-kind counts, top engines and queries, plus configured engines.

tools.name: web_snapshot
tools.description: Render a page in a headless browser (Playwright, optional persisted login state), extract readable text with per-site rules, and save HTML plus an optional full-page screenshot. Returns file paths. Use for JS-heavy pages or when you need a visual capture.

url.description: The HTTP(S) URL to snapshot.

screenshot.description: Save a full-page PNG screenshot (default true).

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

The workflow's identity rides the `meta` parameter as JSON: required `name` (short kebab-case) and `description` strings, optional `whenToUse` string and `phases` array (`{title, detail?, provider?, model?}`). The `script` parameter is the plain JavaScript body ONLY (NOT TypeScript, and NO `export const meta` statement — meta is a parameter, not code), running with top-level await; end with `return <value>` — the value must be JSON-serializable and is this tool's result.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf — no pattern/format/numeric bounds) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides (either may be provided alone). Anything else (`effort`/`isolation`/`agentType`) is rejected loudly.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. An ordinary stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) throw errors that ALWAYS kill the script — they never dissolve into a per-item `null`.

Constraints: concurrency and total-agent caps apply; no filesystem, network, timers, or Node.js APIs are provided — the agents do the work, the script only coordinates them. The run executes in the foreground: this call returns when the whole script finishes.

script.description: The plain-JS workflow script body (top-level await allowed; NO `export const meta` statement; end with `return <json-value>`).

meta.description: The workflow identity block (plain JSON — never code).

name.description: Short kebab-case workflow name.

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

tools.name: write
tools.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.

sandbox_permissions.description: The wider sandbox mode this file operation needs. Only valid as a one-shot retry of an operation the sandbox just denied; requires justification and user approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access.

content.text:
Excellent! Two decisive results:

1. **Wikipedia confirms YOW's coordinates: 45.32250°N, 75.66722°W (45°19′21″N 75°40′02″W)**. My memory was wrong — I had misremembered the coordinates of a different airport (I was thinking of YOW = 45.02, -75.38, but that's probably actually... hmm, whatever, doesn't matter). YOW is at **45.3225N, 75.6672W**, which matches perfectly with wxdb's "OTTAWA INTL A" station_id 49568 at coordinates [-75.67, 45.32]! And Wikipedia also says the airport is "15 km south of downtown Ottawa" — consistent (downtown 45.42 → airport 45.32 = about 11-15 km).

   So **station_id 49568 = OTTAWA INTL A at [-75.67, 45.32] is YOW**. ✓

2. The `wxdb.ca/stations?station_id=49568` query did not filter by station ID — it returned a full list of stations (count=100, cursor present, starting from station_id=2 in British Columbia). In other words, wxdb's `/stations` endpoint does not support the `station_id` parameter (the docs' "Filter by specific station ID" was either wrong or I misread it — maybe that filter is on the /observations endpoint? No... actually, re-reading the docs: "Find stations by location with metadata" — the parameters are only lat/lon/radius/postal_code/bbox/polygon. The "filter by station_id" in the compact summary was probably a hallucination from my earlier reading. In any case, it doesn't matter now.)

So YOW = wxdb station 49568, confirmed via coordinate match (Wikipedia 45.3225N/75.6672W vs wxdb [45.32,-75.67]).

Next: fetch daily observations for station_id=49568 from 2025-11-01 to 2026-09-24 (today). About 328 days → about 328 rows, well within the 5000/page limit.

URL: `https://wxdb.ca/observations/daily?station_id=49568&start=2025-11-01T00:00:00Z&end=2026-09-24T23:59:59Z`

Hmm, one concern: the timezone of `date`. wxdb's dates — are they UTC or local? ECCC observations are usually in local time (ET). The docs example used UTC Z times. Daily features have a "date" property — probably local date (ET) for YOW. My end datetime 2026-09-24T23:59:59Z is UTC = 19:59 ET, so the last ET day that might be included is... hmm. To be safe, I could use end=2026-09-25T00:00:00Z — no wait, that would include part of Sept 25 in UTC, which would be Sept 24 in ET (UTC+... no, ET in September is EDT = UTC-4; so 2026-09-25T00:00:00Z = 2026-09-24 20:00 EDT). So end=2026-09-25T00:00:00Z captures all of Sept 24 ET without touching Sept 25. And start=2025-11-01T00:00:00Z = Nov 1 04:00 EDT — hmm, that would cut off the first ~4 hours of Nov 1 local time!

Hmm. If wxdb's `date` field is ET and the filter is against UTC timestamps... I don't know exactly how wxdb does the filtering (probably it converts to the station's timezone, or filters by date string). To be safe:
- start=2025-10-31T19:00:00Z (= 2025-10-31 15:00 EDT... no wait. UTC-4 → local = UTC+4 hours? No! EDT = UTC-4, so local time = UTC - 4 hours. So 2025-10-31T19:00:00Z = 2025-10-31 15:00 EDT. Hmm, that's before Nov 1 ET.

Let me redo this properly: I want to include all of Nov 1 (ET). Nov 1 00:00 EDT = Nov 1 04:00 UTC. So start=2025-11-01T04:00:00Z would be exactly the local midnight. To be safe, use start=2025-10-31T23:00:00Z (= Oct 31 19:00 EDT) — hmm, that's before local Nov 1... wait no: Oct 31 23:00 UTC = Oct 31 19:00 EDT. That's still Oct 31 ET!

I'm confusing myself. Let me be careful:
- EDT = UTC−4 (Eastern Daylight Time, summer). So local_time = UTC_time − 4h.
- Nov 1 00:00 EDT corresponds to Nov 1 04:00 UTC.
- To include all of Nov 1 in ET, the start must be ≤ Nov 1 00:00 EDT = Nov 1 04:00 UTC. Using start=2025-11-01T00:00:00Z includes everything from Nov 1 00:00 UTC = Nov 1 04:00... wait no!

Ugh, I keep flipping it. Let me be very explicit:
- UTC time T corresponds to local ET time T − 4h (in summer).
- A daily record "2025-11-01" in wxdb represents the ET day Nov 1 (00:00–23:59 EDT), i.e., UTC [Nov 1 04:00, Nov 2 04:00).
- If wxdb filters by UTC timestamp range [start, end):
  - start=2025-11-01T00:00:00Z → includes UTC from Nov 1 00:00 = Nov 30 20:00 EDT. So the "Nov 1" ET day (UTC Nov 1 04:00–05:00... no wait, Nov 1 04:00–05:00 UTC is not a whole day) — hmm, if wxdb assigns each observation to a date by local time, the Nov 1 ET day's observations fall within UTC [Nov 1 04:00, Nov 2 04:00). A filter range [Nov 1 00:00Z, end) includes all of that (since Nov 1 04:00Z > Nov 1 00:00Z). So the entire "Nov 1" ET daily record is included ✓.
  - The only risk with start=2025-11-01T00:00:00Z: it might also include some of the "Oct 31" ET day (UTC Oct 31 04:00–Nov 1 04:00) — specifically UTC [Nov 1 00:00, Nov 1 04:00) = EDT [Oct 31 20:00, Oct 31 24:00). If wxdb's daily aggregation is by ET day, the "Oct 31" record would be a single feature with date=2025-10-31, and its UTC timestamp range [Oct 31 04:00Z, Nov 1 04:00Z) partially overlaps [Nov 1 00:00Z, ...). Whether that feature gets included depends on wxdb's internal logic (whether it checks whether the feature's timestamp is inside the range, or whether the date string falls within the local-time range).

To avoid edge cases, the safest approach: use start=2025-10-31T00:00:00Z? No wait — hmm. Actually, simpler: fetch with the exact UTC boundaries and then **verify from the returned data**: check the first and last `date` values in the response. If the first date is 2025-11-01 and the last is 2026-09-24, perfect. If the first is 2025-10-31 or the last is 2026-09-25, adjust (filter in Python anyway — I'll sum only dates within [2025-11-01, 2026-09-24] regardless).

Actually, since I'm going to filter by date string in Python anyway, the cleanest thing is: fetch with a slightly wider UTC range (start=2025-11-01T00:00:00Z, end=2026-09-25T00:00:00Z), and in Python sum only features where date ∈ [2025-11-01, 2026-09-24]. That handles all edge cases.

Hmm wait, but is wxdb's daily `date` local (ET) or UTC? For YOW, probably local (ECCC reports in local time). If it's UTC, then "2025-11-01" = UTC day Nov 1 = EDT [Oct 31 20:00, Nov 1 20:00) — a slight shift. Either way, my Python date-string filter on the returned features is what matters, and I'll report which dates were included.

OK, let me fetch the data now. URL:
`https://wxdb.ca/observations/daily?station_id=49568&start=2025-11-01T00:00:00Z&end=2026-09-25T00:00:00Z`

About 328 rows. Each feature is probably ~200 bytes → about 70KB of JSON. web_fetch_pro's maxChars default is 50000; set to 150000 to be safe? Hmm, but the result gets returned to me as text — 150K chars is a lot of context. Alternative: fetch and save to file via web_fetch_file! The tool description says: "Fetch a URL and write the body to a FILE in the workspace."

But wait — can I write to /workspace? Current policy: "DSH file policy is workspace-write — files under /workspace are writable". And /tmp was confirmed writable earlier. So `web_fetch_file` with path=/tmp/yow_daily.json (or /workspace). Let me use web_fetch_file to save the JSON to a file, avoiding context bloat. Then parse with python3 (jq not available).

Hmm, one caveat: does web_fetch_file support any path? "Write the body to a FILE in the workspace" — probably under /workspace or a temp directory. Earlier I confirmed /tmp is writable via test.txt... actually, did I create /tmp/test.txt? The summary says "/tmp/test.txt — scratch file confirming /tmp is writable". So /tmp works. Let me use /tmp/yow_daily.json.

Plan:
1. web_fetch_file url=observations/daily station 49568 range → /tmp/yow_daily.json (returns HTTP status).
2. Verify the file exists and check its size; peek at head/tail to confirm dates and fields.
3. Python script: parse JSON, filter date ∈ [2025-11-01, 2026-09-24], sum total_snow_cm (handle nulls), count days, report min/max date, missing-day count, cm + mm.
4. Compose final answer in Chinese: method, data source (wxdb.ca → ECCC observations; note that api.weather.gc.ca's old REST is decommissioned and blocked; GeoMet OGC API exists but the host was blocked this session), process, result with future-dated caveat (Oct–Dec 2026 has not occurred yet; today = 2026-09-24).

Also cross-check: wxdb daily `total_snow_cm` — is this "snowfall" (snow that fell) or "snow depth"? ECCC's daily snow variables: in the climate data, "Snowfall (cm)" is a valid variable. wxdb's field name total_snow_cm suggests accumulated snowfall for the day. Good enough; I'll describe it as "daily snowfall".

Also note: some days may have null/missing total_snow_cm — treat as 0 but report count of missing values. Also check whether there are any days with zero snow... not needed.

Let me also consider monthly aggregation: wxdb has /observations/monthly, which might give a pre-aggregated monthly total_snow — could be a good cross-check on the same page (fetching monthly for Nov 2025–Sep 2026 = 11 rows). That would be a nice verification. Let me do that after the daily fetch.

OK, executing step 1 now: web_fetch_file.

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`. Attempting a command the sandbox may deny is safe and expected: run it and read the marker rather than assuming the denial. When a command is denied and a wider mode would let it succeed, escalate immediately in the same turn — the one sanctioned exception to a denial: retry the exact same command once with `sandbox_permissions` (the narrowest wider mode that suffices) plus a one-sentence `justification`. Do not detour through chat to ask permission first — the approval prompt raised by that retry is how the user consents. If the session states approval prompts are disabled, there is no exception: a denial is final — do not set `sandbox_permissions`. Never escalate speculatively: ground the request in a real denial — normally the one this command just hit; escalating up front is fine only when this session already denied the same access. A rejected escalation is final for that command — stop and explain, never work around it — but it does not forbid attempting or escalating other commands later.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap, and kills the command on expiry.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

sandbox_permissions.description: The wider sandbox mode this command needs. Only valid as a one-shot retry of a command the sandbox just denied; requires justification and user approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact command needs the wider access.
